title: ActiveRecord::ConfigurationError on has many through with conditions
body:
Hi there,

Hope this is not user error and an actual issue! We're testing out edge and I believe the `ActiveRecord::ConfigurationError` is being raised unnecessarily on a `has_many through` with a clause. `project.contacts` works as expected. Also, version Rails 6.0.3.3 does not raise.

I can get the test below to pass if I change the `ordered` scope from:

```ruby
order(Arel.sql("users.first_name || ' ' || users.last_name ASC"))
```

to

```ruby
order(Arel.sql("first_name || ' ' || last_name ASC"))
```

We usually try to reference the table name when writing SQL to avoid ambiguous column references. Should we avoid doing that in the future?

Thanks for your time!

### Steps to reproduce
```ruby
# frozen_string_literal: true

require 'bundler/inline'

gemfile(true) do
  source 'https://rubygems.org'

  git_source(:github) { |repo| "https://github.com/#{repo}.git" }

  # Activate the gem you are reporting the issue against.
  gem 'rails', github: 'rails/rails'
  gem 'sqlite3'
end

require 'active_record'
require 'minitest/autorun'
require 'logger'

# This connection will do for database-independent bug reports.
ActiveRecord::Base.establish_connection(adapter: 'sqlite3', database: ':memory:')
ActiveRecord::Base.logger = Logger.new(STDOUT)

ActiveRecord::Schema.define do
  create_table :contacts, force: true do |t|
    t.integer :user_id
    t.integer :project_id
  end

  create_table :users, force: true do |t|
    t.text :first_name
    t.text :last_name
  end

  create_table :projects, force: true do |t|
  end
end

class Project < ActiveRecord::Base
  has_many :contacts, -> { ordered }
  has_many :users, through: :contacts
end

class User < ActiveRecord::Base
  has_many :contacts

  scope :ordered, -> { order(Arel.sql("users.first_name || ' ' || users.last_name ASC")) }
end

class Contact < ActiveRecord::Base
  belongs_to :user
  belongs_to :project

  scope :ordered, -> { joins(:user).merge(User.ordered) }
end

class BugTest < Minitest::Test
  def test_configuration_join_error_bug
    project = Project.create!
    user_one = User.create!(first_name: 'Zach', last_name: 'Doe')
    user_two = User.create!(first_name: 'Alice', last_name: 'Smith')
    contact_one = Contact.create!(user: user_one, project: project)
    contact_two = Contact.create!(user: user_two, project: project)
    assert_equal [contact_two, contact_one], project.contacts
    assert_equal [user_two, user_one], project.users
  end
end
```

### Expected behavior
I expect both `project.contacts` and `project.users` to not raise an error, and be returned in order as specified by the scope on User.

### Actual behavior
